reason: Several non-obvious rules about how agent prompts are served (store wins over file, intake pinned never stored, prompt.sent depends on collect) were learned this episode and exist only in the memory graph; the next session editing a prompt needs them in a loaded skill.

The episode checked that the store-served system prompt matched the shipped one by comparing the two readers directly. That check is the proof that serving through the store changed nothing, and the escaped `>` display is a known quirk that will otherwise look like a bug.

The memory dandelion investigation found the relate rule sat in on-demand instructions that agents never read, while every pushed text said only to attach a memory to its node. The rule about where prompts land belongs here.

A placement rule is worded in several served texts of the dispatch prompts (the work record and the numbered Knowledge Update and memory steps). Rich's 2026-10-15 correction changed the rule from "decide the depth" to "record where you found it; the link settles itself". Editing one copy leaves the others telling agents the old rule, so the skill needs a pitfall saying every served copy changes together and each one is checked.
The placement wording in served prompts is being superseded (agents no longer judge depth); the skill is where an editor will look, so the copies that must change together are named here.
